topic: MP HC: a dowry demand made after marriage is punishable even without any prior agreement on the amount - Sections 2 and 4, Dowry Prohibition Act; demand can be proved by oral evidence (D.B. v. State of M.P., 2026:MPHC-IND:28859, 2026 LiveLaw (MP) 419)

slides.title: Dowry demand after marriage? **Still a crime**
slides.subtitle: No earlier deal on the amount is needed. Asking for more money **after** the wedding is itself punishable.
slides.cite: **D.B. v. State of M.P.**, 2026:MPHC-IND:28859 · Justice Alok Awasthi

slides.label: The case
slides.title: **Rs 8 lakh more** after the wedding
bullets: At the 2007 marriage, the bride's family gave jewellery, household items and **₹17 lakh**.
The husband's side allegedly said they had expected **₹25 lakh**, demanded the remaining **₹8 lakh**, and harassed her over it.
The trial court convicted the husband and father-in-law. The Sessions Court **acquitted** them.

slides.label: What the court said
slides.title: The **demand itself** is the offence
bullets: Dowry covers property given or agreed to be given **before, at, or any time after** the marriage, if it is linked to the marriage.
Section 4 does **not** need a prior agreement fixing the amount or articles.
A dowry demand can be proved by **oral evidence**. No written proof is required.
slides.note: **Law fact:** Demanding dowry under Section 4 can mean jail from **6 months to 2 years** and a fine up to **₹10,000**.

slides.label: The result
slides.title: Husband's conviction **restored**
bullets: The High Court set aside the acquittal and restored his conviction under **Section 498A IPC** and **Section 4** of the Dowry Act.
Sentence: **one year** of rigorous imprisonment and a fine. He must surrender within **seven days**.
Small differences in witnesses' dates or words do not make the core story false.
slides.note: **Law fact:** For offences from 1 July 2024, cruelty by husband or relatives is **Section 85, BNS**.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Every case turns on **evidence**
bullets: The demand must be **connected with the marriage**. The court still checks whether the evidence is reliable.
A wife does not have to file a separate police complaint for **every incident**. Trying to settle first does not weaken her case.

caption:
Asking for more dowry after the wedding is still a crime ⚖️💍

The Madhya Pradesh High Court has said that a dowry case does not need proof of any deal on the amount made before the marriage. Under Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, dowry includes property given or agreed to be given before, at, or any time after the marriage, if it is connected with the marriage. So a demand raised after the wedding is covered, and the demand itself is the offence under Section 4.

In this case, the bride's family had given ₹17 lakh, jewellery and household items at the 2007 wedding. The husband's side allegedly said they had expected ₹25 lakh and harassed her for the remaining ₹8 lakh. The trial court convicted them, but the Sessions Court acquitted them. The High Court set aside the acquittal and restored the husband's conviction under Section 498A IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Act, with one year of rigorous imprisonment and a fine. The appeal against the father-in-law ended because he had died.

The court also said a dowry demand can be proved by oral evidence, minor differences in witnesses' accounts do not destroy the core case, and a wife need not file a police complaint for every incident. Each case still depends on its own evidence.

Case: D.B. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2026:MPHC-IND:28859 | 2026 LiveLaw (MP) 419 | Justice Alok Awasthi, MP High Court (Indore)
